pr_body:
Summary of the changes (Less than 80 chars)
Zero allocation version of the MediaTypeHeaderValue.IsSubsetOf implementation. The method takes StringSegment to produce a result and only makes type/subtype comparison.

Closes #21265
pr_comments:
MVC has a struct version of this type called MediaType. I think that lets you avoid the need to allocate a new object. Unfortunately it lives in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Formatters namespace.

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/master/src/Mvc/Mvc.Core/src/Formatters/MediaType.cs
Allocating a MetdiaTypeHeaderValue shouldn't be a concern if it's global rather than per request.

Sure, I'm not objecting to that.

I wonder whether we need this when kind of already have a non-allocating version of this API via MediaType.

issue_context.title: New overload of MediaTypeHeaderValue.IsSubsetOf with zero allocations
issue_context.body:
Suggested by @Tratcher in https://github.com/microsoft/reverse-proxy/pull/80#discussion_r414696103

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
Code duplication. The gRPC server stack, and now YARP, are doing this by hand.

### Additional context
Code locations that would benefit from this:
* YARP: [GRpcProtocolHelper.IsGRpcContentType](https://github.com/microsoft/reverse-proxy/pull/80#discussion_r414696103)
* gRPC server stack: [CommonGrpcProtocolHelpers.IsContentType](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-dotnet/blob/3ce9b104524a4929f5014c13cd99ba9a1c2431d4/src/Shared/CommonGrpcProtocolHelpers.cs#L26)
comments: Triage: Seems legit ;). Let's do it.

I want to work on this one.

I will add a new overload `MediaTypeHeaderValue.IsSubsetOf(StringSegment)`. Parse and IsSubsetOf methods use StringSegment and don't allocate unless media type has parameters like text/plain;charset=utf-8;foo=bar;q=0.0. 
If media type has parameters, MediaTypeHeaderValue stores key/value pairs in Parameters collection.

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/master/src/Http/Headers/src/MediaTypeHeaderValue.cs#L183

In this scenario, IsSubsetOf(StringSegment) needs to allocate to store and compare parameters. Any suggestions on this one?
IsSubsetOf doesn't need the parameters to produce an answer. It could stop parsing when it reaches the first parameter.

IsSubsetOf(MediaTypeValue) compares paramaters to produce an answer. https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/master/src/Http/Headers/src/MediaTypeHeaderValue.cs#L395 

Are you saying that the new overload doesn't need to compare the parameters?
We're not considering parameters in the gRPC examples above. Maybe we shouldn't be overloading IsSubsetOf but should do a different method like MatchesMediaType that doesn't consider parameters.

What about throwing an exception if the parameter contains parameters and direct users to use the other overload? or adding parameter support to the new overload for the feature parity? MatchMediaType name may be misleading because the method actually performs IsSubSetOf operations.
No, throwing for a common situation makes the API hard to use.
I understand. I agree with doing a different method then. If this is the final decision, I can start working on it :)
Give it a try and we'll see how it works. Thanks

We've moved this issue to the Backlog milestone. This means that it is not going to be worked on for the coming release. We will reassess the backlog following the current release and consider this item at that time. review_comments: A secondary assertion to add here would be to create a MediaTypeHeaderValue for mediaType2 and assert that you get the same result for parsedMediaType2.IsSubsetOf(parsedMediaType1).
I added IsSubsetOf result comparison to all test methods.

```suggestion
        [InlineData("application/entity", "application/entity+")]
        [InlineData("application/entity+*", "application/entity+json")] // We don't allow suffixes to be wildcards
```
What happens here if plus was the last character?
The suffix will equal to {}. I copied that behavior from the parse method. Should I change it?
Ok, I just wanted to be sure it didn't throw an index out of bounds exception.

How much does ordering matter here? 

Take this scenario we're trying to replace:
https://github.com/grpc/grpc-dotnet/blob/3ce9b104524a4929f5014c13cd99ba9a1c2431d4/src/Shared/CommonGrpcProtocolHelpers.cs#L26
https://github.com/grpc/grpc-dotnet/search?q=IsContentType&unscoped_q=IsContentType
Or here:
https://github.com/microsoft/reverse-proxy/blob/419c4d6502d1e8510a6dd0a0bedd67fa410ec1f2/src/ReverseProxy/Utilities/ProtocolHelper.cs#L30

You'd want one pre-parsed MediaTypeHeaderValue that you're comparing all incoming headers against. If there's a wildcard, it's always in the original value, not in the second value you're comparing to.
So, `MediaTypeHeaderValue.Parse("*/*").MatchesMediaType("text/plain")` should return true and `MediaTypeHeaderValue.Parse("text/plain").MatchesMediaType("*/*")` should return false right?

Sorry I let this go stale. Please let me know if you're interested in continuing or not.

Yes, you've described the desired behavior.
Yes, I'm still interested in contributing. It looks like I need to make some changes to invert comparisons and remove unnecessary test cases. I'll let you know when I finish the implementation.
Can you take a look at it again? @Tratcher
